pr_body:
Using a placeholder argument for the SQL string makes it so any escaping
that is needed is automatically handled in the database when the
argument is parsed, rather than needing to do it in the workload code.

This also fixes the constraintIsDropping check to also check if the
constraint is being added. Dropping the constraint in either states
is not fully supported, as per:
https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/a3b0aa3902155b01470c4c512d23f201c8b18f7c/pkg/sql/catalog/tabledesc/structured.go#L1271-L1278

Finally, when creaing the DROP CONSTRAINT command itself, the constraint
name needs to be treated as an identifier so it gets double-quoted.

fixes https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/127273
Release note: None

issue_context.title: workload/schemachange: constraintIsPrimary should consider colname fuzzing
issue_context.body:
```	
Received unexpected error:
***UNEXPECTED ERROR; Failed to generate a random operation: CollectOne: Query: "\n\tSELECT EXISTS(\n\t        SELECT *\n\t          FROM pg_catalog.pg_constraint\n\t         WHERE conrelid = 'public.table_w0_41'::REGCLASS::INT\n\t           AND conname = 'table_w0_41_col41_w0_44_co'l4%q1_w0_42_key'\n\t           AND (contype = 'p')\n\t       );\n\t" []: ERROR: at or near "l4": syntax error (SQLSTATE 42601)
(1) forced error mark
...
Wraps: (6) CollectOne: Query: "\n\tSELECT EXISTS(\n\t        SELECT *\n\t          FROM pg_catalog.pg_constraint\n\t         WHERE conrelid = 'public.table_w0_41'::REGCLASS::INT\n\t           AND conname = 'table_w0_41_col41_w0_44_co'l4%q1_w0_42_key'\n\t           AND (contype = 'p')\n\t       );\n\t" []
Wraps: (7) ERROR: at or near "l4": syntax error (SQLSTATE 42601)
```

Theory: the constraint name was automatically generated from the column name -- which is fuzzed. We should find a way to handle this, but lexbase.EscapeSQLIdent doesn't seem to work in this case. Here is the table if needed:
```
   "sql": "CREATE TABLE public.table_w0_41 (\"co'l4%q1_w0_42\" FLOAT8 NOT NULL, \"col4\t1_w0_43\" BOOL NULL, col41_w0_44 STRING NOT NULL AS (lower(CAST(\"col4\t1_w0_43\" AS STRING))) VIRTUAL, PRIMARY KEY (col41_w0_44), INDEX (\"co'l4%q1_w0_42\" ASC, col41_w0_44) STORING (\"col4\t1_w0_43\"), INDEX (abs(\"co'l4%q1_w0_42\") ASC) STORING (\"co'l4%q1_w0_42\"), UNIQUE (col41_w0_44), INDEX (\"co'l4%q1_w0_42\"), UNIQUE (\"col4\t1_w0_43\" ASC), UNIQUE (\"col4\t1_w0_43\" DESC) STORING (\"co'l4%q1_w0_42\"), UNIQUE (col41_w0_44 DESC, \"co'l4%q1_w0_42\" DESC), FAMILY (\"co'l4%q1_w0_42\", \"col4\t1_w0_43\"))"
```


Jira issue: CRDB-40350

Epic CRDB-19168
comments: The proper function to use for SQL strings is `lexbase.EscapeSQLString`. The `EscapeSQLIdent` function is meant for identifiers in the syntax. For example in `CREATE TABLE t (a INT, b STRING)`, `t`, `a`, and `b` are all identifiers. But if you are ever comparing a name to a SQL value, like in `conname = 'table_w0_41_col41_w0_44_co'l4%q1_w0_42_key'`, that is a SQL string. (In that case, since the SQL string has single quotes in it, those quotes need to be escaped, which is what `EscapeSQLString` will do.)
